title: OpenAI pursues acquisition of Trail of Bits security firm
content:
OpenAI is pursuing an acquisition of Trail of Bits, a security company that specialises in finding and fixing security vulnerabilities in open-source software, The Information reported on Oct. 13 local time.
OpenAI is holding early acquisition talks with Trail of Bits, the report said. The size of the deal is not known. Talks are ongoing and could fall apart, The Information said sources told it.
This year, OpenAI and Anthropic have competed over developing specialised AI to find software vulnerabilities. Trail of Bits would help OpenAI expand its security business, The Information said.
Trail of Bits, founded in 2012, has also supported maintenance of open-source projects.
Trail of Bits launched a software patch project, Patch the Planet, with OpenAI in June. Trail of Bits employees are using OpenAI Codex and security-focused models to find and fix bugs in open-source projects such as Python. Dan Guido (댄 귀도), Trail of Bits' CEO, said, "Thanks to Codex, we were able to deliver in a day what would have taken weeks."
OpenAI has also recently hired Dally Rajic (달리 라직), a former executive at Google-owned cloud security company Wiz, as chief revenue officer.

report.summary: OpenAI is reportedly in early talks to acquire Trail of Bits, an open-source security firm, to strengthen AI-driven vulnerability discovery and fixing.
report.background: OpenAI and Anthropic have spent much of 2025 competing to build AI that can find software vulnerabilities, turning automated code auditing into a strategic battleground. Trail of Bits, founded in 2012, is a well-known security firm that audits critical software, fixes open-source vulnerabilities, and maintains open-source projects. In June, it launched Patch the Planet with OpenAI, using OpenAI Codex and security-focused models to find and patch bugs in projects such as Python. Trail of Bits CEO Dan Guido said Codex let the team deliver in a day work that would normally take weeks. OpenAI also recently hired a former Wiz executive as chief revenue officer. The talks fit a broader push by AI labs into cybersecurity, where model-driven bug hunting and patching could become both a safety mission and a commercial product.
key_points: OpenAI is in early acquisition talks with Trail of Bits, The Information reported. No price has been disclosed, and sources say the deal could still fall apart. If completed, it would give OpenAI a proven security services team and deeper ties to the open-source security community.

Trail of Bits, founded in 2012, specialises in finding and fixing vulnerabilities in open-source software. It also supports maintenance of open-source projects, giving it credibility and reach across critical infrastructure, developer tools, and programming languages. That expertise is hard to replicate quickly.

The two organisations already work together. Their June Patch the Planet project uses OpenAI Codex and security models to patch open-source bugs, including in Python. Trail of Bits CEO Dan Guido said Codex helped deliver in one day what would have taken weeks, a strong signal of AI's growing role in security work.

The move would intensify competition with Anthropic, which has also pushed AI for vulnerability discovery. OpenAI appears to be building an enterprise security offering, reinforced by hiring a former Wiz executive as chief revenue officer. That suggests monetisation, not just research, is the goal.

For the open-source ecosystem, having a major AI lab acquire a trusted security auditor raises questions about independence, disclosure practices, and who controls critical vulnerability research. Supporters see faster patches; critics worry about concentration of security power in a few AI companies.
report.impact: For the AI industry, the reported deal signals that cybersecurity is becoming a core frontier for large model providers. It could accelerate AI-driven code audit and patching, but also concentrate vulnerability intelligence inside a few companies. For developers, AI-assisted tools may find and fix bugs faster, lowering maintenance burden; yet they should watch for false positives, opaque model decisions, and over-reliance on proprietary systems. For regular users, the upside is safer software and quicker patches for widely used open-source components; the downside is that security decisions may become less transparent. Open-source maintainers could gain resources, but they may also face new governance and funding dependencies.
report.tools: Watch OpenAI Codex and OpenAI's security-focused models, plus Trail of Bits' Patch the Planet initiative. Developers can also try Trail of Bits' open-source security tools, including Slither for Solidity static analysis, Echidna and Medusa for smart-contract fuzzing, and Manticore for symbolic execution. These projects show how AI and traditional program analysis may combine in future vulnerability research.
